subject: Finding K in an exponential growth model

messages.author: 9839c75e5703f57c
messages.subject: Finding K in an exponential growth model
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm modeling the larval abundance of the fire salamander in five different streams. For this I am using replicated count data over 11 weeks. All streams will be analyzed separately.
I am doing this with the pcountOpen() function and with the dynamics = "trend", to get a model for exponential growth.
I am now struggling to find the right value for K.
My maximum count in one stream for example is 44.
To find K, I did some simulations by setting in different K values in my pcountOpen model.
With the dynamics = "constant" it seems as if it was enough to set K = 62. On the other hand, when I set dynamics = "trend", I can hardly find the right K, because it would be much over 400. This seems rather too high to me.

My question is:
Does someone know why the exponential growth model requires such a high K value respect to the "constant" model?

Kind regards,
Michelle

messages.author: 9839c75e5703f57c
messages.subject: Re: Finding K in an exponential growth model
parts:
To find K, I generated a a loop that fills in different K's into the Null model.

ks <- seq(1*Kmin+1, 5*Kmin, Kmin/5)
Abun <- numeric(0)
for(t in ks) {
  m <- pcountOpen(~1, ~1, ~1, ~1, data = umf1, K=t, se = FALSE, dynamics = ("constant"), mixture = "NB")
  r <- ranef(m)
  a <- bup(r)
  Abun <- rbind(Abun, a)
}


ks <- seq(1*Kmin+1, 10*Kmin, Kmin/2)
Abun <- numeric(0)
for(t in ks) {
  m <- pcountOpen(~1, ~1, ~1, ~1, data =  umf1, K=t, se = FALSE, dynamics = ("trend"), mixture = "NB")
  r <- ranef(m)
  a <- bup(r)
  Abun <- rbind(Abun, a)
}
